name: Moyobe / mɔyɔbɛ
confidence_why: Rongier 1996 and Pali 2011 both describe Miyobe as a tone language in which a high versus low tone on the verb marks aspect, and neither mentions word stress; they differ only on whether a third, mid tone level exists, and only excerpts of Rongier 1996 and the abstract of Pali 2011 are available.

catalog_quote: Une étude morphotonologique s'avère bien entendu indispensable . Je n'ai pas trouvé d'oppositions permettant de poser l'existence de trois tons . Par contre, l'abaissement du ton haut est fréquent . Il semble systématique dans les verbes bi- ou trisyllabiques à la forme inaccomplie, lorsque les deux dernières syllabes sont de tons hauts . Le dernier est alors abaissé et s'oppose au ton bas de l'accompli lorsque la forme est par ailleurs similaire . nè wéésí [ nè wé : s1 ] “ je cherche " nè wéésì [ nè wé : sì ] “ j'ai cherché " nè símésí [ nè símési ] " je parle " [ nè símésì ] " j'ai parlé " ... [Pali 2011, thesis abstract:] Sur le plan tonal, trois niveaux se distinguent : haut, moyen et bas.

new_statements.translation: ... tone. A morphotonological study is of course indispensable. I have found no oppositions that would allow positing the existence of three tones. On the other hand, lowering (downstep) of the high tone is frequent. It seems systematic in bi- or trisyllabic verbs in the imperfective form, when the last two syllables are high-toned: the last one is then lowered and contrasts with the low tone of the perfective ... [Pali 2011 abstract:] On the tonal level, three levels are distinguished: high, mid and low.

new_statements.rule_in_words: Miyobe is described as a tone language (Rongier 1996: two level tones H/L with frequent, grammatically conditioned downstep of H; Pali 2011: three levels H/M/L). No opened or snippet-visible source says anything about word stress or accent; snippet searches for 'accent', 'accentuation', 'intensité', 'accent tonique' inside Rongier 1996 and Person 1955 returned nothing.
new_statements.secondary_stress: Not mentioned in any accessible text.
new_statements.exceptions: The two sources disagree on the number of tone levels (Rongier: no evidence for a third tone, but systematic downstep; Pali: three levels H, M, L) — Pali's 'mid' may correspond to Rongier's downstepped high, but this cannot be checked without the full texts.
new_statements.domain_note: Rongier's downstep remark concerns bi-/trisyllabic verb forms (imperfective vs perfective); Pali's statement is a thesis-abstract summary of the tonal system of the language, domain unspecified. The quoted text comes from Google Books snippets and an official thesis abstract, not from a page opened by me; no page locator is available.
new_statements.identity_note: All sources refer to the same language miyo1238 under different names: mɔyɔbɛ/moyobe (Rongier 1996), miyobé (Pali 2011), biyobè/uyóbè/Soruba (Person 1955), Sol(l)a (exonym, Güldemann 2018). Rongier's snippet mentions correcting an earlier 'solla' wordlist whose terms were 'souvent si éloignés de la réalité'. No dialect is specified in any accessible text; Ceccaldi 1979 (Gallica) cites Person for a 'Minatyire' dialect 'très proche du miyobe'.

new_statements.quote: En phonologie, le miyobé se caractérise par la non pertinence des traits de longueur, de nasalité ainsi que du trait [ATR] pour les voyelles. De même, au niveau consonantique, l'opposition Voisé/non Voisé n'est pas phonologique. Dans la syllabe, le noyau a le trait de centralité résultant de son contraste avec l'absence ou la présence d'une marge. Sur le plan tonal, trois niveaux se distinguent : haut, moyen et bas. [...] Les marqueurs aspecto-temporels sont des flexifs tonals et des spécificatifs.
new_statements.translation: In phonology, Miyobé is characterised by the non-relevance of the features of length, nasality and [ATR] for vowels. Likewise, at the consonantal level the voiced/voiceless opposition is not phonological. In the syllable, the nucleus has the centrality feature resulting from its contrast with the absence or presence of a margin. On the tonal level, three levels are distinguished: high, mid and low. [...] The aspecto-temporal markers are tonal inflectional morphemes and specifiers.

new_statements.relation_note: Same statement the catalog already leans on (existing_statements cites this abstract as corroboration of 'tone language, no stress statement'), so it agrees. The full 575-page thesis, which is where a stress/accent section would be, could not be opened: theses. same result in the earlier round), SUDOC PPN 271856734 marks the PDF 'Accès réservé au texte intégral', and the Bordeaux Montaigne diffusion link redirects to CAS login. HAL and Google Books (two no-preview ANRT-type records) have no copy. Note that the abstract's three tone levels differ from Rongier 1996, who found no oppositions justifying three tones; this is a tone-inventory difference, not a stress difference.
new_statements.rule_in_words: Miyobé is a three-level tone language (H, M, L) in which tone also carries aspect marking; the abstract says nothing about word stress or accent.
new_statements.identity_note: All sources concern the same language (Miyobé/mɔyɔbɛ, ISO soy, Glottolog miyo1238) as spoken in Togo and Benin; no work opened names a particular dialect. Rongier 1996 writes 'mɔyɔbɛ/moyobe', Pali 2011/2014 'miyobé'.

new_statements.quote: En effet, le ton porté par yɛ est un marqueur aspectuel (Pali, 2011). Il est H (haut) à l'aspect inaccompli et B (bas) à l'aspect accompli.
new_statements.translation: Indeed, the tone carried by yɛ is an aspect marker (Pali 2011). It is H (high) in the imperfective aspect and L (low) in the perfective aspect.

readall_conflicts: No source opened says anything about word stress, so there is no stress conflict. The only disagreement among sources is the tone inventory: Rongier 1996 (existing snippet) found no oppositions establishing three tones and describes frequent lowering of H, whereas Pali 2011's abstract posits three levels (high, mid, low); Pali 2014 uses only H and B (L) in its examples. Neither listed work could be read in full: Gblem-Poidi & Kantchoa 2012 has no viewable pages at the listed Google Books id and the preview edition is bot-blocked; Pali 2011's full text is restricted despite theses.fr flagging it accessible.
